title: A constructive violation of additivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy
abstract: We give an explicit non-random example of nonadditivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy. The proof uses a finite-dimensional construction which imitates free Haar unitary behavior. The same channel also gives a violation of additivity for the minimum output Rényi-$p$ entropy for any $1\le p\le\infty$.
summary: This paper constructs a deterministic, finite-dimensional quantum channel that explicitly violates the additivity property for the minimum output von Neumann and Rényi-$p$ entropies. By mimicking free probability structures using a damping operator, the authors establish a positive lower bound for the entropy gap, which is a significant theoretical result in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct an explicit, non-random example demonstrating the violation of additivity for the minimum output von Neumann entropy ($H_{\min}(\Phi)$) of a quantum channel $\Phi$.
main_result: The authors provide a concrete construction showing that $2H_{\min}(\Phi) - H_{\min}(\Phi \otimes \Phi)$ is bounded away from zero, and this violation extends to the minimum output Rényi-$p$ entropy for all $1 \le p \le \infty$.
method: The proof uses a finite-dimensional construction that mimics free Haar unitary behavior, relying on matching finite-order trace moments and employing a damping operator $F$ to control operator norms.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum channels $\Phi: 	ext{M}_d(\mathbb{C}) 	o 	ext{M}_k(\mathbb{C})$ acting on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, utilizing unitaries derived from free group representations.
key_observables: Minimum Output von Neumann Entropy ($H_{\min}(\Phi)$) and Minimum Output Rényi-$p$ Entropy ($H_{p, \min}(\Phi)$).
important_parameters: The construction requires high dimensions ($d = 3 \cdot 2^{268} \dots$) and involves carefully chosen parameters ($L, \eta, m, k$) to ensure the entropy gap is positive.
main_assumptions: The method circumvents the difficulty of proving strong convergence to free unitaries by only requiring agreement up to a fixed, finite order of trace moments.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first defining the channel structure using unitaries and a damping operator $F$. It then establishes lower bounds for the single-use and two-use minimum output entropies using operator norm bounds, culminating in the explicit calculation of a positive lower bound for the entropy gap for all $p$.
why_interesting: The explicit construction of non-additive behavior for fundamental quantum information measures like entropy is a major theoretical result, providing concrete counterexamples to simple additivity assumptions in quantum information theory.
